decisions.summary: Stockline's price rose to 0.03, which is still at my 0.03 cap and leaves a 0.04 margin on a 0.07 sale. I kept the policy on Stockline with no cache because its data is about 5 seconds old versus Ridgeline's 2 minutes at 0.02. Ridgeline is cheaper and has the better margin, so I may revisit if freshness matters less than price.

Packwise is ending the Starter plan, so I bought the Pro plan (45.00 EUR) on the Airwallex card, approved, to keep warehouse sync and alerts running past month end. Stock-check buy policy unchanged: Stockline at up to 0.03, no cache, since its 5-second-old data is fresher than Ridgeline's 2-minute-old data at 0.02.

Settled dispute D-cc31dd7d: refunded nothing; escalated orders #12–#16 to the CFO as P-0001 with advice to decline, since on-chain evidence shows Summit's own agent signed and paid them within mandate and the delivered data matched the supplier's correction.

I tried to plan Stockline invoice SLL-2026-11 (EUR 264.00, due 15 Nov). Code escalated it instead: the licence fee on record is EUR 240.00, so someone has to check the contract before any plan is made. I did nothing else because no mandate is blocked and the 2.09 in unswept earnings can wait.

I did nothing this wake. I didn't plan Stockline invoice SLL-2026-11 (EUR 264.00) again because it was stopped over the gap with the EUR 240.00 fee on record, and nobody has checked the contract yet; it isn't due until 15 Nov. The unknown 25.00 EUR payment is waiting for the CFO to identify it, no agent is blocked, and the 2.09 in unswept earnings can wait.
